subject: Architecture
title: Apple Park: Silicon Valley's Spaceship
description: A 60-second lesson on Apple Park: Silicon Valley's Spaceship.

hook.text: Apple Park is a single ring-shaped building with a circumference of nearly one mile.

buildup.text: Steve Jobs personally briefed Norman Foster and obsessed over details like doorknob shapes.

discovery.text: The building's curved glass panels are the largest ever made — each one custom-manufactured.

twist.text: Jobs died before construction began. The campus is his last product, built exactly to his vision.

climax.text: Nine thousand trees surround the building. The site generates more energy than it uses.

punchline.text: He designed computers, phones, and finally a building. All the same way.

quiz.question: What happened to Steve Jobs before Apple Park was built?
options: He retired and moved to Japan
He changed the design to a rectangular building

details.summary: Apple Park in Cupertino, designed by Norman Foster, is a 260,000-square-meter ring-shaped building housing 12,000 employees around a 12-hectare central courtyard. Its curved glass panels — the largest ever fabricated — required custom manufacturing processes.
details.whyItMatters: Apple Park demonstrates that corporate architecture can embody a company's philosophy. Steve Jobs envisioned a campus that felt like nature rather than an office park, and the result blurs the boundary between building, landscape, and technology.
takeaways: Ring-shaped building houses 12,000 employees around a courtyard
Custom-fabricated curved glass panels are the largest ever made
The building generates more energy than it consumes

faq.question: Why is Apple Park ring-shaped?
faq.answer: Steve Jobs wanted a building where every office had a view of nature. The ring shape ensures all workspaces face either the central courtyard or the surrounding landscape. The form also facilitates natural ventilation — the building needs no heating or air conditioning for nine months of the year.

faq.question: How does Apple Park generate its own energy?
faq.answer: The roof holds 17 megawatts of solar panels — one of the largest corporate solar installations in the world. Biogas fuel cells provide backup power. On most days the campus produces more electricity than it uses, sending surplus back to the grid.
